subject: Post-activation quickcheck: KV warm, ACL drift, routing smoke
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Alice White <alice.white@acme-payments.com>
Cc: ops@ascendcloud.io
Date: 2026-12-09T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: Post-activation quickcheck: KV warm, ACL drift, routing smoke

Team / Acme,

We just completed the cutover window for the VPC private deployment. This thread is to capture the immediate sanity checks and short evidence so we can close the activation checklist. Please do the quick checks below and reply with results inline. I want to capture anything that needs rollback or a 1-hour follow-up bridge.

Quick checklist (15-30m tasks):
- KV cache priming: confirm percent of keys warmed (target >= 90%) and any nodes under 70%
- ACL drift: confirm intended firewall rules present; flag any unexpected denies
- Routing/BGP: confirm peer sessions up and no packet-loss >1% on production paths
- Service health: 1-minute success rate for token route and prompt route >= 99%

Attachments: post-activation-runbook-v3.pdf (runbook excerpt), kv-priming-summary-20261209.csv (initial prefill stats).

If anything is red, include a minimal rollback path and who to call. If green, please reply with a short one-line confirmation and paste the most relevant line from your instrumentation (eg. "KV primed: 92% hit-rate on node g4-12").

I'll be on standby in the activation channel and can open a bridge if needed.

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Sr. Ops Lead, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Alice White <alice.white@acme-payments.com>
Date: 2026-12-09T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-activation quickcheck: KV warm, ACL drift, routing smoke

Rafael — quick status from infra checks: 

- KV cache priming: overall 93% keys warmed across pool. Two pods briefly reported lower fill (g4-7 at 68%, g4-9 at 71%) but prefill retried and both are now 91% and 89% respectively. See kv-priming-summary-20261209.csv for per-node lines.
- ACL drift: No unexpected denies. Verified expected management ranges + Acme peer subnets in NACLs.
- Routing: Primary paths green. Observed 0.4% packet loss on transit->edge for 5m window at 08:50 but dropped to 0.0 after route reflap suppressed. No impact to app-layer success. Attached a short tcpdump slice as tcpdump-acme-peer-1215.log (filtered).
- Service health: token route 99.6% (1m), prompt route 99.2% (1m).

Action items: Marcus, please review the two pods that had initial lower priming and confirm prefill script exit codes. If we see a persistent <85% we should consider a retry with adjusted concurrency.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Cloud Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Alice White <alice.white@acme-payments.com>
Date: 2026-12-09T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-activation quickcheck: KV warm, ACL drift, routing smoke

On 2026-12-09 09:22, Hannah Schmitt wrote:
> - Routing: Primary paths green. Observed 0.4% packet loss on transit->edge for 5m window at 08:50 but dropped to 0.0 after route reflap suppressed. No impact to app-layer success.

Adding a brief note — saw a TTL mismatch reported by the eBPF hop tracer on two transit hops which correlates with the 08:50 window. I pushed a conservative firewall delta to allow the transient ICMP type for trace (rule ID fw-allow-icmp-trace-612) and that cleared the tracer alerts. No customer traffic was affected.

Rollback path: remove fw-allow-icmp-trace-612 (undo script: ./infra/acl/undo-fw-allow-icmp-trace-612.sh) if any side-effects observed. I documented the change in the runbook (section 4.3).

— Irene
Irene Choi
Principal Network Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Alice White <alice.white@acme-payments.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-09T13:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-activation quickcheck: KV warm, ACL drift, routing smoke

Thanks all — Acme side quick readout: BGP peering had two quick flaps during the transition window (08:46–08:51) while our edge announced the new /24s; sessions recovered and have been stable since 08:52. We saw some SYN retransmits at 08:50 but no application errors at our end.

We confirm matching ACLs and no rejects from our firewall logs. KV priming numbers on our side look consistent with Hannah's report. No incidents to escalate from Acme.

— Alice White
Sr. SRE, Acme Payments
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Alice White <alice.white@acme-payments.com>
Date: 2026-12-09T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-activation quickcheck: KV warm, ACL drift, routing smoke

Couple of follow-ups from the KV side:
- Root cause for the two lower-fill pods was a short-lived NFS stall during prefill; prefill process retried successfully. I pushed a minor prefill tweak (lower concurrency on nodes g4-7/g4-9) which improved stability — change is in the commit linked below.
- Recommend we bump the prefill concurrency ceiling by 10% for pooled nodes during the next low-traffic window to avoid re-runs; I will open a short RFC for the change.

Reference: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-prefill/commit/9f4a2b (change: add retry/backoff to prefill worker)

If no objections, I'll schedule the RFC and include a one-line rollback (revert commit 9f4a2b).

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Alice White <alice.white@acme-payments.com>
Cc: ops@ascendcloud.io
Date: 2026-12-09T16:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-activation quickcheck: KV warm, ACL drift, routing smoke

Thanks team — wrapping up the thread: 

- Status: Activation accepted. KV priming passed (>=90% overall), ACLs verified, routing stable post-flap, service success rates within SLO.
- Open actions: Marcus to open RFC for prefill concurrency bump (owner: Marcus). Irene to keep fw-allow-icmp-trace-612 in the active list for 24h and then remove if no anomalies (owner: Irene). Hannah to attach final per-node CSV in the evidence bundle.
- Evidence: I've packaged the runbook excerpt, the kv CSV, and tcpdump slice into evidence-bundle-final.zip and uploaded to the activation artifacts folder (link in HubSpot).

If anyone sees regressions overnight, escalate to the on-call bridge and tag me. Otherwise I'll close the activation checklist by EOD.

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Sr. Ops Lead, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
